Landing.title: From your sketch to the right workshop.
Landing.subtitle: Describe your furniture with its exact dimensions, and verified workshops compete with structured offers. You compare revisions and choose.

Landing.partnersSub: Every workshop is vetted before it can quote. Ratings come from Google reviews.

SketchGuidePage.title: How to sketch your space
SketchGuidePage.subtitle: No architect needed — four simple steps give workshops everything they need to quote accurately. The sheet on the left shows exactly what your sketch needs to include.
SketchGuidePage.legendWall: The wall, measured corner to corner — width and height
SketchGuidePage.legendSocket: Sockets and pipes, marked with ✕ or a dashed circle
SketchGuidePage.legendFurniture: The furniture you want, drawn simply over the wall
SketchGuidePage.legendDimensions: The furniture dimensions, noted right on the drawing

measure.title: Measure the walls
measure.body: Take the length of every wall and the ceiling height. Measure at floor level, corner to corner.
measure.tip: A simple tape measure is enough — round to the centimetre.

draw.title: Draw the plan from above
draw.body: A simple rectangle is enough. Write each dimension right on its side, like in the example.
draw.tip: It doesn't have to be to scale — the numbers matter, not pretty drawing.

mark.title: Mark what can't move
mark.body: Doors with their swing, windows, sockets, pipes, radiators. Anything the future furniture could touch.
mark.tip: An ✕ for sockets, a double line for windows — like the socket mark on the sheet.

photo.title: Photograph and attach
photo.body: One clear photo, from above, with the whole sketch in frame. Attach it to your request along with photos of the room.
photo.tip: Natural light, no shadows over the numbers.

SketchGuidePage.ctaHint: Attach it while configuring your request — workshops receive it along with your dimensions.

info.title: Melamine chipboard
info.body: Melamine-faced chipboard — the best price/durability ratio for cabinet bodies.
info.cons1: Edges less refined without ABS banding
info.cons2: Sensitive to moisture on unsealed cuts

MDF.label: MDF
MDF.description: Painted or foil fronts, premium look

info.title: Painted/foiled MDF
info.body: Medium-density fibreboard — ideal for painted, milled or foil-wrapped fronts.

MDF_INFOLIAT.label: Foil-wrapped MDF
MDF_INFOLIAT.description: PVC foil on routed fronts, easy to maintain

info.title: Foil-wrapped MDF
info.body: MDF fronts covered with heat-pressed PVC foil — allows routed profiles with a clean look at a moderate price.
info.cons1: Foil can peel near strong heat

info.title: Painted MDF
info.body: Electrostatically painted MDF fronts — any RAL colour, in matte, satin or gloss finish.

MDF_FURNIR.label: Veneered MDF
MDF_FURNIR.description: Natural wood veneer on a stable core

info.title: Veneered MDF
info.body: MDF covered with natural wood veneer — authentic wood grain without the warping risk of solid timber.
info.pros3: Can be stained in different shades
info.cons1: Rare veneers cost close to solid wood

info.title: Solid wood
info.body: Natural timber — the most durable and valuable option, with unique grain.

ALTUL.label: Other
ALTUL.description: Type the material you want below

otherMaterial.title: What material do you have in mind?
otherMaterial.subtitle: Briefly describe the material or finish you want — the workshop will confirm availability.

pieceSystems.title: Which opening system?
pieceSystems.subtitle: For this piece's doors and drawers — you can pick several.

info.title: Push-to-open
info.body: Open with a simple press, no handles — minimalist look.

info.title: Sliding systems
info.body: Doors or drawers on rails — save space, ideal for wardrobes.

info.title: Press latch
info.body: Simple click mechanism — the most economical handleless opening option.

MANER.label: Handle
MANER.description: Applied handles, your choice of model

info.title: Classic handles
info.body: Handles mounted on the fronts — from minimal to classic, the model is chosen with the workshop.

info.title: Gola profile
info.body: Aluminium channel integrated between fronts — you open from the profile and the front line stays uninterrupted.

AVENTOS.label: Aventos (lift-up)
AVENTOS.description: The front lifts vertically, with soft-close

info.title: Aventos system
info.body: Wall-cabinet fronts lift upwards on damped arms — full access, no door at head height.
info.pros1: Easy access, no door to bump into

layout.title: What layout is the kitchen?
layout.subtitle: Pick the configuration that fits your space.

info.title: Straight kitchen
info.body: All cabinets on one wall — compact, suited to small spaces.

info.title: L-shaped kitchen
info.body: Cabinets on two walls — a good balance of worktop and circulation.
info.cons1: Corner can be hard to reach

info.title: U-shaped kitchen
info.body: Cabinets on three sides — maximum storage and worktop.

info.title: Galley kitchen
info.body: Two parallel runs — efficient for pass-through kitchens.

hasIsland.title: Do you want an island?
hasIsland.subtitle: An island adds worktop, storage and a serving spot.

info.title: Kitchen island
info.body: A freestanding unit in the middle — needs at least 1.2 m clearance on each side.

dimensions.title: A few dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: Measure the length of the runs and the room height.

cabinetZones.title: Which cabinet zones?
cabinetZones.subtitle: Pick the cabinet types you need.

frontMaterial.title: Front material?
frontMaterial.subtitle: The material drives the look and price.

frontMaterialBase.title: Front material for the base units?
frontMaterialBase.subtitle: The lower cabinets — the material drives the look and price.

frontMaterialWall.title: Front material for the wall units?
frontMaterialWall.subtitle: The upper cabinets can use a different material.

frontMaterialIsland.title: Front material for the island?
frontMaterialIsland.subtitle: The island can stand out with its own material.

openingSystemsBase.title: Opening system for the base units?
openingSystemsBase.subtitle: You can pick several.

openingSystemsWall.title: Opening system for the wall units?
openingSystemsWall.subtitle: You can pick several.

sketch.title: Upload your project or sketch
sketch.subtitle: Optional — a sketch or plan for this kitchen helps firms quote accurately.

countertop.title: Which countertop?
countertop.subtitle: Optional — helps the firm estimate more accurately.

info.title: Laminated chipboard worktop
info.body: Chipboard core with a laminated surface — the affordable standard, many designs.

info.title: HPL worktop
info.body: High-pressure laminate — far denser and more resistant to water and scratches than standard boards.

info.title: Laminate countertop
info.body: Laminated chipboard — affordable with many finishes.

info.title: Quartz countertop
info.body: Engineered stone — very durable and hygienic.

info.title: Granite countertop
info.body: Natural stone — durable, with unique texture.

info.title: Wood countertop
info.body: Solid wood — warm look, needs periodic oiling.

appliances.title: Built-in appliances?
appliances.subtitle: Optional — helps with cut-outs and niches.

extraPieces.title: Extra pieces
extraPieces.subtitle: Optional — add special units or accessories.

notes.title: Anything else?
notes.subtitle: Optional — any preference or note for the firms.

pieces.title: What pieces do you need?
pieces.subtitle: Add each piece with its material and quantity.

sketch.title: Upload your project or sketch
sketch.subtitle: Optional — a sketch or plan helps firms quote accurately.

info.title: Linear closet
info.body: Modules on a single wall — compact.

info.title: L-shaped closet
info.body: Modules on two walls — good balance.

info.title: U-shaped closet
info.body: Modules on three sides — maximum capacity.

info.title: Walk-in closet
info.body: A dedicated room with modules on several walls.

info.title: Sliding doors
info.body: Doors on rails — no opening space needed.

info.title: Hinged doors
info.body: Classic hinged doors — full access to the interior.

info.title: Open closet
info.body: Doorless modules — quick access, airy look.

interiorModules.title: Interior modules?
interiorModules.subtitle: Pick at least one module — the interior layout.

info.title: Hanging rods
info.body: The classic hanger zone. One meter of rod holds about 10-12 hangers; long dresses need 150-160 cm of free height.

info.title: Drawers
info.body: The priciest interior module: slides, fronts, assembly. Soft-close drawers are worth it in daily-use zones.

info.title: Shelves
info.body: The most affordable modules. Adjustable shelves are a small extra that pays off quickly.

info.title: Shoe rack
info.body: Tilted shelves with a stopper or pull-out racks. Allow about 20 cm of width per pair.

info.title: Interior accessories
info.body: Pull-out trouser rack, belt and tie holders, wire baskets. Easy to add later, but cheaper if planned from the start.

LED_LIGHTING.label: LED lighting
LED_LIGHTING.description: LED strip with a door sensor

info.title: LED lighting
info.body: LED strip under shelves or along the sides, usually with a door or motion sensor. Needs power nearby — tell the company where the closest outlet is.

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling dressing
info.body: Modules go all the way up: no dust collecting on top and you gain seasonal storage. Needs careful measuring — ceilings are rarely perfectly level.
info.cons1: Top zone needs a step stool

lighting.title: Integrated LED lighting?
lighting.subtitle: LED strip with a door sensor.

info.title: LED lighting
info.body: LED strip under shelves or along the sides, usually with a door or motion sensor. Needs power nearby — tell the company where the closest outlet is.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch of the space?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — a simple sketch with measurements helps companies quote precisely.

info.title: Sliding doors
info.body: Doors glide on tracks — no clearance needed, ideal when the bed sits close to the wardrobe.
info.cons1: Only half the wardrobe visible at a time

info.title: Hinged doors
info.body: Classic doors on hinges — full access to the interior and lower cost. Need ~50 cm of clearance in front.

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling wardrobe
info.body: The unit goes all the way up: no dust on top, seasonal storage above. Needs the ceiling height measured in several spots.
info.cons1: Top zone needs a step stool

bedSize.title: What mattress size?
bedSize.subtitle: The bed is built around the mattress.

info.title: Standard mattress sizes
info.body: Standard sizes in Romania: 90x200 (single), 140x200 (compact double), 160x200 (the standard double), 180x200 (king). The mattress is NOT included.

CUSTOM.label: Custom dimensions
CUSTOM.description: Enter your mattress width and length

info.title: Simple bed
info.body: Classic frame, no mechanisms. The most affordable and easiest to move.

info.title: Gas-lift base
info.body: The mattress lifts on gas pistons revealing a full-size storage box underneath. The biggest hidden storage in the bedroom.

info.title: Under-bed drawers
info.body: Two to four drawers accessible from the side, without lifting the mattress. They need clear space next to the bed.

info.title: Upholstered bed
info.body: Frame and headboard wrapped in fabric or eco-leather — a soft look with many color options. The exact fabric is chosen with the company.

info.title: One or a pair
info.body: A pair costs nearly double but looks balanced next to a double bed. For a single bed, one is enough.

sketch.title: Do you have a room sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the room plan with the bed and wardrobe positions.

OTHER.label: Something else
OTHER.description: A piece that is not in the list

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: Width and height of each piece.

tvStyle.title: What does the TV area look like?
tvStyle.subtitle: Floating, on the floor, or a full unit with cabinets.

info.title: Floating TV unit
info.body: A horizontal unit fixed to the wall — the floor stays clear and the look is airy.
info.cons1: Needs a solid wall for mounting

ON_FLOOR.label: On the floor
ON_FLOOR.description: Unit standing on legs or a plinth

info.title: Floor-standing TV unit
info.body: Classic and versatile: storage for electronics and media, with the TV on top or wall-mounted above.

info.title: TV unit with cabinets
info.body: A full-wall composition: TV unit with cabinets or columns on the left and right, often with a niche and LED lighting.

piecesOtherText.title: What piece do you have in mind?
piecesOtherText.subtitle: Briefly describe the piece that is not in the list.

ledLighting.title: LED lighting in the furniture?
ledLighting.subtitle: LED strip in panels or units.

info.title: LED lighting
info.body: Warm LED strip behind TV panels or inside display cabinets. Needs an outlet nearby.

ledPieces.title: Which units get LED lighting?
ledPieces.subtitle: Tick only the units that get an LED strip — you can skip this.

info.title: LED lighting
info.body: Warm LED strip behind TV panels or inside display cabinets. Needs an outlet nearby.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch of the space?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the TV wall with measurements and outlets marked.

info.title: Straight desk
info.body: A worktop along one wall — compact and flexible. For comfortable work we recommend at least 120 cm width and 60 cm depth.

info.title: Corner desk
info.body: Two work sides — one for the monitor, one kept clear. Uses the room corner that would otherwise be wasted.

info.title: U-shaped desk
info.body: Worktop on three sides — a complete workstation with everything within a chair's spin.

info.title: Organizing the cables
info.body: A metal tray under the worktop plus discreet cutouts. The desk stays clean and vacuuming stops being an adventure. Tell the company how many monitors/devices you have.

sketch.title: Do you have a room sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the working wall, with outlets and the window marked.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: The width of each selected piece, plus ceiling height.

info.title: Why ventilation matters
info.body: In a bathroom without ventilation, humidity builds up and affects furniture. In that case we recommend MDF, which resists moisture better — but the final choice is yours.

info.title: Bathroom material
info.body: We recommend painted or foiled MDF, resistant to humidity. Avoid unsealed chipboard in areas exposed to water.

materialVanity.title: Material for the vanity unit?
materialVanity.subtitle: The piece most exposed to water.

materialMirror.title: Material for the mirror cabinet?
materialMirror.subtitle: Can differ from the other pieces.

materialTall.title: Material for the tall storage?
materialTall.subtitle: Can differ from the other pieces.

sketch.title: Upload your project or sketch
sketch.subtitle: Optional — a sketch or plan for this bathroom helps firms quote accurately.

depthProfile.title: How wide is the hallway?
depthProfile.subtitle: Furniture depth follows the passage space.

info.title: Why depth matters
info.body: In a narrow hallway every centimeter counts: keep at least 90 cm of free passage. Slim furniture (25–35 cm) uses tilt-out doors and angled racks to fit the shoes.

info.title: Slim units
info.body: Tilt-out shoe cabinet, flat coat panel, mirror — everything under 35 cm deep so the passage stays clear.

info.title: Standard units
info.body: Normal wardrobe depth — hangers sit normally and storage boxes fit.
info.cons1: Needs a hallway over 1.5 m wide

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: The width of each selected piece.

openingSystems.title: Opening systems
openingSystems.subtitle: Optional — for units with doors or drawers.

sketch.title: Do you have a hallway sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — wall lengths and door positions.

applianceSetup.title: How do the appliances sit?
applianceSetup.subtitle: The washer and dryer layout decides the rest.

info.title: Washer only
info.body: A single appliance to build around — the rest of the space goes to storage and worktop.
info.cons1: No dryer, clothes dry on a rack

info.title: Appliance column
info.body: The dryer sits on top of the washer in a dedicated cabinet with a support shelf. Takes only 60–70 cm of width.

info.title: Side by side
info.body: Washer and dryer next to each other under a continuous worktop — a generous surface for sorting and folding.

ventilation.title: Is the room ventilated?
ventilation.subtitle: Laundry humidity matters when choosing materials.

info.title: Why ventilation matters
info.body: The washer and dryer release moisture. Without a window or fan, steam builds up and affects the furniture — in that case we recommend foil-wrapped MDF, which handles humidity better.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: The main wall and ceiling height.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch of the space?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — water hookups and outlet positions help a lot.

wallsUsed.title: How many walls do we use?
wallsUsed.subtitle: The shelving layout in the pantry.

info.title: Moving around the pantry
info.body: Keep at least 80 cm free between shelves so you can move and see what is on them. In a narrow pantry, single-wall shelving is the right call.

storageStyle.title: Open or closed storage?
storageStyle.subtitle: Open shelves, cabinets with doors, or a mix.

info.title: Open shelves
info.body: The most practical and affordable pantry option: you see everything at a glance.

info.title: Cabinets with doors
info.body: Items stay protected from dust and everything looks tidy, even when it is not.

info.title: Combination
info.body: Closed cabinets below for rarely used items, open shelves above for daily access — the practical balance.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: The length of each shelved side.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: The pantry is a utility space — PAL offers the best value here.

sketch.title: Do you have a pantry sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — wall sizes and the door position.

enclosed.title: Is the balcony enclosed?
enclosed.subtitle: Indoor furniture only lasts on an enclosed balcony.

info.title: Why enclosure matters
info.body: PAL and MDF suffer from moisture, frost and direct sun. On a glazed balcony they behave like indoors; on an open one we recommend treated solid wood or rethinking the project.

info.title: Enclosed balcony
info.body: The environment is close to indoors — any material works, minding direct sun which fades fronts over time.

info.title: Open balcony
info.body: Rain, frost, sun — tough conditions for furniture. We recommend exterior-treated solid wood and stainless hardware.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: Usable length and free depth of the balcony.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: See the recommendation based on the balcony type.

sketch.title: Do you have a balcony sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — length, depth and window positions.

doorType.title: What doors for the wardrobe?
doorType.subtitle: The access system changes price and required space.

info.title: Sliding doors
info.body: Doors glide on tracks — no opening clearance needed. Quality tracks make the long-term difference.
info.cons1: Only half the wardrobe visible at a time

info.title: Hinged doors
info.body: Doors on hinges — full access and lower cost. Need ~50 cm of clearance in front of the wardrobe.

toCeiling.title: Up to the ceiling (dressing-style)?
toCeiling.subtitle: The wardrobe goes all the way up, like a built-in dressing.

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling wardrobe
info.body: Built-in look, no dust on top, seasonal storage above. Requires measuring the height in several spots — ceilings are rarely level.
info.cons1: Top zone needs a step stool

sketch.title: Do you have a wall sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — wall width and obstacles (outlets, radiator, door).

config3d.title: Build your wardrobe in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Choose the width, split the columns and decide each zone: hanging rod, shelves, drawers or doors.

style.title: Low unit or media wall?
style.subtitle: From a simple unit to a full-wall composition.

info.title: Low TV unit
info.body: A horizontal unit with doors and drawers — electronics and media hidden away, TV above.

info.title: Full media wall
info.body: A complete composition: decorative panels, suspended units, a TV niche and usually LED lighting. Cables vanish behind the panels.

info.title: TV on the wall or on the unit
info.body: If the TV is wall-mounted, the company prepares the cable route and possibly a niche. If it sits on the unit, the top depth matters. You can also decide later, together with the company.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: The width of the TV area.

sketch.title: Do you have a wall sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — wall width and outlet positions.

config3d.title: Build your TV unit in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Adjust the dimensions and pick each zone: open, drawers or doors.

style.title: What bookcase style?
style.subtitle: Open, with base cabinets, or glass doors.

info.title: Open bookcase
info.body: Simple shelves, instant access to books. Needs regular dusting — the books are exposed.

info.title: With base cabinets
info.body: Closed doors below for less sightly things, open shelves above for books and decor.

info.title: Display bookcase
info.body: Glass doors over the full height — books and objects stay dust-free and visible.

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling bookcase
info.body: A full wall of books — striking and efficient. The top row needs a step stool.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: Wide shelves need a rigid material.

sketch.title: Do you have a wall sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — wall width and ceiling height.

config3d.title: Build your bookcase in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Drag the sliders and click zones — the model updates live, and workshops receive your exact configuration.

shape.title: What desk shape?
shape.subtitle: Straight along a wall or L-shaped in a corner.

info.title: Straight desk
info.body: A worktop along one wall — compact. For comfortable work: at least 120 cm wide, 60 cm deep.

info.title: Corner desk
info.body: Two work zones and a well-used corner. Ideal with two monitors or when you need a clear writing area.

info.title: Organizing the cables
info.body: A tray under the worktop and discreet cutouts — the desk stays clean. Tell the company how many devices you have (monitors, laptop, chargers).

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: Worktop width (and side B if L-shaped).

storage.title: Desk storage?
storage.subtitle: Optional — a drawer unit or a shelf riser.

DRAWER_UNIT.label: Drawer unit
DRAWER_UNIT.description: Under the top, fixed or mobile

info.title: Drawer unit
info.body: Three-four drawers under the worktop, fixed or on wheels. Home for documents and small items.

info.title: Shelf riser
info.body: Shelves above the desk for books and files — you use the wall, not the worktop.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: The desktop gets scratched first — the finish matters.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch of the space?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the working wall, with outlets and the window.

config3d.title: Build your desk in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Choose the top and configure the pedestals with drawers or doors.

bedSize.title: What mattress size?
bedSize.subtitle: The bed is built around the mattress.

info.title: Standard sizes
info.body: Romanian standards: 90x200 (single), 140x200 (compact double), 160x200 (double), 180x200 (king). The mattress is NOT included.

info.title: Upholstered bed
info.body: Frame and headboard wrapped in fabric or eco-leather. Fabric and color are chosen with the company.

info.title: Simple bed
info.body: Classic frame with no mechanisms — the most affordable.

info.title: Gas-lift base
info.body: The mattress lifts on gas pistons; underneath, a full-size storage box. The biggest hidden storage.

info.title: Under-bed drawers
info.body: Two-four drawers on the sides — quick access to linens without lifting anything.
info.cons1: Needs clear space beside the bed

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: The frame material (for upholstered beds, the inner structure).

sketch.title: Do you have a room sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the bed position in the room.

info.title: Drawer dresser
info.body: The bedroom classic — everything organized by level. Soft-close drawers are worth it here.

info.title: Mixed dresser
info.body: Drawers on one side, doors with shelves on the other — flexible for differently shaped items.

info.title: Door dresser
info.body: Doors with interior shelves — the most affordable option, good for bulky items.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the wall where the dresser will sit.

config3d.title: Build your dresser in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Adjust the dimensions and split the body into drawers, doors or open zones.

tableType.title: What kind of table?
tableType.subtitle: The purpose decides size and height.

info.title: Rectangular table
info.body: The classic shape — fits against a wall or centered, easy to place in any room.

info.title: Round table
info.body: Friendly in small spaces and with kids — no corners. For the same seat count it needs a bit more room around it.

info.title: Extendable table
info.body: Compact day to day, extends by 40–80 cm for guests. A good mechanism makes the difference — ask the company what hardware they use.

info.title: Seats and sizes
info.body: As a guide: 4 people → 120–140 cm; 6 people → 160–180 cm; 8+ → over 200 cm. Allow ~60 cm of width per person.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: The tabletop works hardest — solid wood is the favorite here.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the space where the table will sit.

style.title: What type of shoe cabinet?
style.subtitle: The mechanism decides depth and capacity.

info.title: Slim shoe cabinet
info.body: Tilt-out doors with angled racks — shoes stand vertically. Perfect for narrow hallways.
info.cons1: Less capacity; tall boots do not fit

info.title: Classic shoe cabinet
info.body: Horizontal shelves — boots and boxes fit too. Needs a bit more hallway space.

info.title: Shoe cabinet with bench
info.body: A low unit with a seat (often upholstered) and storage below — comfortable shoe changes.

sketch.title: Do you have a hallway sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the available hallway space.

config3d.title: Build your shoe cabinet in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Choose the dimensions and the fronts: tilt-out, drawers or doors.

style.title: What nightstand style?
style.subtitle: With drawers, open shelf or wall-mounted.

info.title: Drawer nightstand
info.body: The classic — small things stay hidden. A soft-close drawer wakes no one at night.

info.title: Open nightstand
info.body: A simple shelf — book and phone within reach. The most affordable option.

info.title: Floating nightstand
info.body: Floats on the wall — airy look and easy cleaning underneath. Needs a solid wall for mounting.

info.title: One or a pair
info.body: A pair looks balanced next to a double bed; for a single bed, one is enough.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: Usually matched to the bed or wardrobe.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the space next to the bed.

config3d.title: Build your nightstand in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Adjust the dimensions and pick the mix of drawers and open zones.

style.title: What type of bench?
style.subtitle: With storage, shoe space, or simple.

info.title: Storage bench
info.body: The seat lifts to reveal a full storage box — blankets, seasonal shoes, toys.

info.title: Bench with shoe rack
info.body: An open rack under the seat — everyday shoes within reach, no doors to open.

info.title: Simple bench
info.body: A clean, minimal piece — just the seat. Works at the foot of the bed or in the hallway.

info.title: Upholstered seat
info.body: A fixed cushion wrapped in fabric — comfortable shoe changes. The fabric is chosen with the company.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the space where the bench will sit.
